issues.detail: Covers the main error-handling path but omits edge cases such as graceful shutdown, malformed JSON body errors (bodyParser 400/413 handling), and CORS origin configuration for production.

scenarios.name: koa-orders-api-with-error-handling
scenarios.rationale: A meets almost every rubric point: error middleware registered first using try/await next()/catch with err.expose, the named import from @koa/bodyparser, ctx.throw(400) validation, and routes() plus allowedMethods(). B misses most of them. It uses the default import from koa-bodyparser instead of the named export from @koa/bodyparser. It never uses err.expose or ctx.throw/ctx.assert, because it validates with zod and sets the status by hand. Its error handler is first and it mounts routes() with allowedMethods(), but that covers only a small part of the rubric.

scenarios.name: express-login-route-migration
scenarios.rationale: B uses ctx.throw(401, ...), explains that rejected promises propagate to error middleware instead of next(err), and names @koa/bodyparser, while A only uses the ctx.status/ctx.body alternative, names koa-bodyparser rather than @koa/bodyparser, and gives a weaker explanation of error propagation.

scenarios.name: upgrade-koa2-router-to-koa3
scenarios.rationale: B covers every rubric item (async rewrite and koa-convert removal, regex param replaced by validation or router.param(), named wildcard, ctx.back(), Node 18+ and 20+), while A leaves out ctx.back(), suggests a manual referrer redirect, and omits the @koa/router 15 Node 20+ requirement.
